items.text: A CLI close of a window's last pane is proven never to ask and never to leave a ghost window on Windows.
A burst of window resizes outside an edge drag no longer redraws the whole pane background on every step.
The title bar and tab strip repaint only when a paint reaches them, and keep their buffers between paints.
The perf baseline now names which threads wake the idle app and what each pane open-close cycle leaves behind.
A spinner title in a folded pane no longer repaints the whole window, only its strip.
The Activity Monitor refreshes on one parked thread instead of starting a new one every 1.5 seconds.
A pane gives back its full-size snapshot once the fold, drag or hero carousel that needed it is over.
Each Windows terminal pane commits about 2 MB less memory: pages come one at a time instead of in 1.5x-grown arena blocks.
A window restored from maximized gives back the memory its maximized size took.
A minimized viewer pane stays minimized when its page grabs focus - now proven on Windows.
Panes minimized into blades on Windows stay minimized after a relaunch, as on the Mac.
